explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-a-judge against human evaluation using correlation analysis on the same set of dialogues, reporting both Pearson and Spearman correlation metrics

prompts.notes: Full prompt shown in appendix Figure 20 with detailed consistency criteria: alignment with initial intent, logical information flow, and contextual relevance

guidelines.notes: Human evaluators scored dialogues on consistency using 10-point scale, following same criteria as LLM judge, but exact human evaluation guidelines not detailed

sample_size.notes: 50 dialogues randomly selected from each benchmark (LIGHT and TOPDIAL) were evaluated by both LLM and human annotators

validation_results.summary_finding: Paper reports strong alignment between LLM and human evaluations with average Spearman correlation of 0.68, surpassing alternative NLG evaluation methods

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluators assessed the same chat consistency criteria: alignment with initial intent, logical information flow, and contextual relevance across turns
